title: Replace a hand-rolled read_dir recursion with walkdir filter_entry
summary: A recursion that walks into target and hidden directories becomes WalkDir pruned with filter_entry, and a root of "." that pruned itself is let through by depth.

turns.user: the .rs collector goes all the way into target, and .git too. slow. someone said use walkdir

assistant.body: Sure! Here's the key point: filter and filter_entry are not the same. filter only drops items from the iterator, so walkdir still descends into target after you reject it. filter_entry skips a directory that returns false, contents and all, without reading it. Hidden directories and target are pruned with filter_entry, and the .rs check stays in filter. Note: filter_map(Result::ok) quietly throws away entries that could not be read.

Apologies, my previous is_skipped also judged the root. WalkDir yields the root itself as an entry at depth 0. "." has no file name, so file_name falls back to the whole path, which is ".", and starts_with('.') pruned the entire walk on the first entry. Entries at depth 0 now always pass.
